data.title: S. Stegmann-Rajtár: Preliminary results of the excavation at Žibrica (excavations in 2002–2003 and 2005–2006)
data.excerpt: We present an article by the archaeologist Susanne Stegmann-Rajtár, a short summary of the insights gained from the excavation of the Žibrica hillfort in recent years. The pottery from the occupation layers places the main phase of Lusatian occupation not only in the Final Bronze Age but also in the Early Hallstatt period, and Early Scythian bronze arrowheads were found on the crown of the rampart.
data.metaDescription: Preliminary results of the archaeological excavation of the Štitáre-Žibrica hillfort near Nitra in 2002–2006, as presented by S. Stegmann-Rajtár.

blocks.text: As early as during the archaeological and geophysical survey in 1999, the most abundant find material was obtained from surface collection at the Štitáre-Žibrica hillfort, Nitra district, and test trenching was therefore subsequently carried out there as well. Besides numerous fragments of Lusatian culture pottery, so-called Early Scythian bronze arrowheads of the Hallstatt period were also found at this site. Two of them came directly from the crown of the rampart in the southern part, one from the immediate vicinity of the inner face of the rampart in the western part. A larger quantity of them is said to come from this hillfort. During the repeated surveys in 2000 and 2001, besides pottery of the Late Urnfield period, sherds of the Hallstatt period were also found, which indicated that occupation here continued in this period as well. On the basis of stray finds it was possible to attest occupation of the La Tène period, the Middle Ages and the modern period as well.

blocks.text: According to Dr Stegmann-Rajtár, the aim of the excavations at the Štitáre-Žibrica hillfort in 2002 and 2003 was to establish the overall time span of the occupation and also to gain insights into the stratigraphy of the occupation layers. The excavation was carried out on one of the most extensive terraces in the north-eastern part of the inner enclosure of the hillfort, where intensive occupation could be expected. The presence of settlement features was also indicated by the results of the geophysical survey and of sounding bores. From the investigated occupation layers I and II a large number of sherds was obtained, above all from the Final Bronze Age and the Early Iron Age; sherds of the La Tène period, the Middle Ages and the modern period occurred here only sporadically. The layers also contained a quantity of daub and animal bones, as well as several pieces of charcoal. Beneath the stone-and-earth bank at the edge of the terrace several sherds were found which can provisionally be assigned to the Čaka culture.

blocks.text: Dr Stegmann-Rajtár goes on to state that although the sherd material comes only from the occupation layers, it provides important information on the cultural and chronological attribution of this site. The pottery is very distinctive, containing a large number of decorated sherds as well as fragments of various characteristic vessel types. The assemblage obtained has given us the first significant insights into the main phase of occupation at the Lusatian culture hillfort, which falls not only in the Final Bronze Age but also in the Early Hallstatt period. The occupation of the hillforts in the Tríbeč range in the Hallstatt period had long been assumed, but until now more substantial find material such as that from Žibrica was lacking. Comparable pottery forms, as well as decorative motifs, are also known from nearby settlements of the same period situated on slopes or in the lowlands, for example at Štitáre-Panská hora or at Nová Ves nad Žitavou. Parallels to the amphorae with a graphite-coated surface and the characteristic decoration of multiple horizontal, vertical or arched grooves such as those from Žibrica also come from numerous Lusatian culture cemeteries of the Late and Final Urnfield period, for example from Partizánske or from Andač. The forms and the decoration of the Hallstatt period pottery from Žibrica have parallels above all at sites of the north-eastern Hallstatt culture.
blocks.source: STEGMANN-RAJTÁR, S.: Die slowakisch-deutschen Ausgrabungen auf der befestigten Höhensiedlung Štitáre-Žibrica (Kr. Nitra). In: Popelnicová pole a doba halštatská.
